summary: SSE stream exhibits recurring micro-pauses then client-side timeout when routed through corporate proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (HelixCare) reports that Server-Sent Events (SSE) chat streams intermittently pause for short bursts (approx 3-8s) every ~30-90s when requests are routed through their corporate reverse proxy. After a few of these pauses the client triggers a request timeout and the SSE connection is closed. The same chat sessions from the same network succeed when the corporate proxy is bypassed (mobile hotspot).

Impact:
- Multiple agents at HelixCare experiencing degraded chat UX during standard workflows.
- Estimated ~25% of streaming sessions for this customer in us-west show at least one micro-pause; ~7% result in client-timeout and reconnect.
- Customer is on a Dedicated plan and is using our VPC peering with an upstream customer-managed proxy.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (dedicated pool for customer) in us-west.
- Client transport: SSE over HTTP/1.1 via customer reverse proxy (NGINX 1.20.x) -> corporate firewall -> Redwood API Gateway (ALB) -> Serving runtime (gpus).
- Affected model: gpt-open-12b-quant pinned to v2026-02-28 build.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start a new chat session using SSE endpoint with keepalive disabled on client side (default SDK config).
2) Send a prompt that triggers a multi-paragraph streaming response (~600 tokens).
3) Observe streaming progress for ~30-120s.
4) After several seconds of visible output, SSE stream pauses for 3-8s, then resumes. After 2-3 pauses the client times out and closes the connection.

Logs / Observations provided by customer:
- Client logs show "SSE: no data for 15s -> timeout" before disconnect.
- Customer provided tcpdump traces at their proxy edge showing bursts of small TCP packets followed by retransmits correlated with pause windows.
- Their NGINX access logs show a single long-running request; error logs show no explicit upstream 502/504.
- On tests without the corporate proxy (mobile hotspot), the same requests stream continuously with small token-level latency spikes but never the multi-second pauses.

Investigation notes (Redwood):
- Reproduced with internal test harness by inserting an NGINX reverse proxy configured with proxy_buffering on and default proxy_busy_buffers_size. When proxy_buffering is enabled and upstream sends many small chunks, observed buffering/coalescing behavior that leads to delivery pauses until buffers flush.
- Captured pcap between proxy and gateway shows Nagle/coalescing behavior at TCP level when small chunks are emitted and outgoing socket has delayed ACKs configured on proxy host. Pauses line up with buffer flush thresholds.
- Our API Gateway (ALB) and serving runtime are emitting SSE chunk frames regularly (verified from server-side request logs and application-level traces). No server-side queueing spike or CPU/GPU pressure observed during reproduced pauses.
- Hypothesis: Corporate proxy + default NGINX buffering + delayed ACKs / TCP_NODELAY interplay causes micro-buffering of SSE chunks, resulting in multi-second pauses from client perspective.

Immediate mitigations to propose to customer:
- Short-term workaround: Use WebSocket transport instead of SSE for streaming through their corporate proxy (customer confirmed WebSocket flows have fewer pauses in quick tests).
- Proxy-side change: Disable proxy_buffering for the SSE endpoint, set proxy_http_version 1.1, add proxy_set_header Connection "" and proxy_request_buffering off / proxy_buffering off, and ensure tcp_nodelay is enabled on the proxy host. For NGINX, set "proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on; tcp_nodelay on;"
- Client-side temporary: Increase SSE client timeout from 15s to 30s to reduce disconnects while root cause is addressed.

Follow-up actions for Redwood (tracking):
- [P0] Create a KB runbook for SSE best-practices when customers place proxies in front of Redwood. Document NGINX and common enterprise proxy adjustments. (owner: Samir P.)
- [P1] Add traffic-level telemetry to detect proxy-induced chunk coalescing (patterns of regular small chunk emission + upstream ACK gap). (owner: Network Observability)
- [P1] Add note to Dedicated onboarding checklist about proxy buffer settings for streaming. (owner: Solutions Engineering)
- [Investigation] Engage with HelixCare networking team to test suggested NGINX settings and validate behavior.

Expected next update: 2026-03-12 with customer test results or a temporary config change applied.
